lines.trans: Tamara, hello, this is Vitya Barinov calling.
Hi, Vitya, do you want to place a bet?
Yes, put money on the Spartak match.
Are you betting on your native Spartak's victory?
No, I am betting on a CSKA victory!
Are you not joking? They are your enemies!
I bet exactly one hundred thousand rubles!
Do you have that kind of money with you?
Reserve the bet, I will bring cash soon.
All right, your bet is accepted at the office.
Thank you, money right now matters more than anything to me.
I hope you understand your huge risk.

беспокоить.gloss: to bother, to disturb; to worry

meanings.note: Privative prefix 'бес-' ('without, -less', before voiceless consonants) (stem 'покоить'). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to bother, to disturb; to worry', paired with 'побеспокоить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to worry (someone)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I don't want to bother you.

examples.text: Мы просто не хотели вас беспокоить. Всё отменим!
examples.trans: We just didn't want to bother you. We'll cancel it all!

meanings.note: the present tense is normally left out: я мэр = I am the mayor
Secondary conversational sense ('there is, there are') (present есть; у меня есть = I have) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
future: буду / будешь ... + infinitive

examples.trans: You will be asking for forgiveness.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'in' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('into, to') (+ accusative (where to)) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: I grew up in a communal flat.
Hello! How was it in Hungary?

meanings.note: Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('important').

examples.text: Я тебе утром говорил: не торопись. Это очень важный вопрос.
examples.trans: I told you this morning: don't rush. It's a very important question.

meanings.note: Russian determiner/pronoun ('all') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.
Secondary conversational sense ('everything') (neuter всё) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('everyone') (plural все) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
end-stressed in oblique forms: врага, врагу

examples.text: С ней вообще нельзя разговаривать. Это наш самый главный враг.
examples.trans: You mustn't talk to her at all. She is our number-one enemy.

meanings.note: emphatic at the start of a sentence
Secondary conversational sense ('? = really?, oh yeah?') (disbelief) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
plural only: there is no singular in everyday use

examples.trans: The money is on the table.
Gum? I didn't have enough money.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'for' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.

examples.trans: We could open a salon for you.

examples.text: Для вас можно открыть салон красоты.
examples.trans: We could open a beauty salon for you.

meanings.note: adds emphasis to the word before it

examples.text: У тебя же есть ещё. Дай хоть одну.
examples.trans: But you've still got some. Give me just one.

meanings.note: Prefix 'за-' marks beginning an action, covering, or stopping by along the way (stem 'резервировать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to reserve', forming an aspectual pair with 'резервировать'.

examples.text: Зарезервируй ставку, я скоро привезу наличные.
examples.trans: Reserve the bet, I will bring cash soon.

meanings.note: to one person you call ты; здравствуйте is the polite form; the first в is silent

examples.text: Здравствуйте, добро пожаловать в наш французский ресторан!
examples.trans: Hello, welcome to our French restaurant!

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'office', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: The bet was accepted at the office.

examples.text: Хорошо, твоя ставка принята в конторе.
examples.trans: All right, your bet is accepted at the office.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'match, game' in everyday Russian.

examples.text: Тихо, Сеня! Сейчас идёт решающий матч!
examples.trans: Quiet, Senya! A decisive match is on right now!

examples.text: Кто сегодня играет на этом матче?
examples.trans: Who is playing in this match today?

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'on' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('onto, to; for') (+ accusative: на второй срок) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: The programme is on the website.
He is running for a second term.

examples.text: Я очень люблю наш город. Поэтому я иду на второй срок.
examples.trans: I love our town very much. That's why I'm running for a second term.

meanings.note: Prefix 'на-' marks surface contact, accumulation, or completing a quantity (stem 'деяться'). Reflexive/intransitive verb with the postfix '-ся'/'-сь' (historically from the reflexive pronoun 'себя', oneself). Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to hope, to rely on', paired with 'понадеяться'.

examples.trans: I hope so. Go on, act quickly!

meanings.note: Declinable plural-only noun meaning 'cash', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Зарезервируй ставку, я скоро привезу наличные.
examples.trans: Reserve the bet, I will bring cash soon.

examples.text: Вот наличные деньги на свежую икру.
examples.trans: Here is the cash for fresh caviar.

meanings.note: goes right before the word it negates
+ genitive: 'у нас нет выбора' = we have no choice
Secondary conversational sense ('there isn't') (+ genitive) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Adjective formed with the common Slavic suffix '-н-' from a noun/verb root. Agrees in gender, number, and case with the noun it modifies ('huge, enormous').

examples.text: Кстати, если хочешь, иди к нам в команду. Шансы у нас огромные.
examples.trans: By the way, if you want, join our team. Our chances are huge.

meanings.note: Declinable feminine noun meaning 'victory', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.text: Люди в городе аплодируют вашей победе!
examples.trans: People in the town are applauding your victory!

meanings.note: понимаешь? = you know? do you understand?

examples.trans: I want to go to the sea, you know?

examples.text: Я хочу нормально жить! Я хочу биде, понимаешь?
examples.trans: I want to live like a normal person! I want a bidet, do you understand?

meanings.note: Prefix 'по-' forms perfective verbs or marks a brief/onset action (stem 'ставить'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to put', forming an aspectual pair with 'ставить'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to install') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Put your foot on the bed.

examples.text: Заходите. Поставьте, пожалуйста, правую ногу на кровать.
examples.trans: Come in. Please put your right foot on the bed.

meanings.note: from a trip, by car, train or plane

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: Expressive conversational Russian interjection or greeting ('hi') used directly in spoken exchanges.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

принять.gloss: to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept

meanings.note: Prefix 'при-' indicates approaching, attachment, or slight degree of action (stem 'нять'). Used as an perfective (single completed action) verb meaning 'to receive, to see (a visitor); to accept', paired with 'принимать'.
Secondary conversational sense ('to accept, to take') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: You recognised me. Thanks for seeing me.

meanings.note: Common masculine noun meaning 'risk' in everyday Russian.

examples.trans: You are afraid of any risk.
You are constantly afraid of any risk.

examples.text: Надеюсь, ты понимаешь свой огромный риск.
examples.trans: I hope you understand your huge risk.

meanings.note: ровно десять секунд = exactly ten seconds
Secondary conversational sense ('evenly, smoothly') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Like a real man, exactly ten seconds.
They cut it exactly in half.

meanings.note: Qualitative or relational adjective formed with the productive '-н-' suffix, meaning 'native' and agreeing in gender, number, and case.
родной брат = full brother; родной город = hometown

examples.text: Ну что, родной мой, за тебя!
examples.trans: Well then, my dear friend, to you!

examples.text: Это будущий мэр Синеозерска! Ну что, родной мой, за тебя!
examples.trans: That is the future mayor of Sineozersk! Well then, my dear friend, to you!

meanings.note: Declinable masculine noun meaning 'rouble', changing its case ending across all six Russian grammatical cases to mark its role in the clause.

examples.trans: I haven't got a single rouble.

examples.text: Наша задача — взять у взяточников миллиард рублей.
examples.trans: Our task is to take a billion roubles from the bribe-takers.

meanings.note: + instrumental; со before some consonant clusters: со всеми

examples.trans: Share it all equally with everyone, understand?

meanings.note: refers back to the subject: 'он держит своё слово' = he keeps his word

examples.text: А что я за мэр такой, который держит своё слово?
examples.trans: And what kind of mayor would I be if I kept my word?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'делать'). Used in Russian as an perfective verb focusing on a single completed action or result meaning 'to do', forming an aspectual pair with 'делать'.

examples.text: Мы сделали много, но надо сделать ещё больше.
examples.trans: We've done a lot, but we need to do even more.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('oneself') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.

examples.text: А с Пашей я снова чувствую себя женщиной.
examples.trans: And with Pasha I feel like a woman again.

meanings.note: 'сейчас буду' = I'll be right there
Secondary conversational sense ('in a moment') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Конечно, помогу. Кто у вас сейчас начальник?
examples.trans: Of course I'll help. Who's your boss now?

meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'коро'). Manner/predicative adverb in '-о', derived from the neuter short form of the corresponding adjective.

examples.text: Так, не шумим. Я скоро вернусь.
examples.trans: Right, no noise. I'll be back soon.

meanings.note: спасибо за + accusative = thank you for

examples.text: Спасибо, спасибо! Как вы все знаете, я родился и вырос в Синеозерске.
examples.trans: Thank you, thank you! As you all know, I was born and grew up in Sineozersk.

meanings.en: to put, to place in an upright position
meanings.note: Prefix 'с-' ('together' or 'down from') marks convergence or completion (stem 'тавить'). Used in Russian as an imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to put', forming an aspectual pair with 'поставить'.

examples.trans: Where should I put the plate?
Put the kettle on the table.

examples.text: Успокойтесь, я ещё сделаю! Куда ставить тарелку?
examples.trans: Calm down, I'll make more! Where should I put the plate?

meanings.note: Derived feminine noun formed with a productive Slavic suffix, used in spoken Russian to mean 'bet'.
Secondary conversational sense ('rate') (wage or interest rate) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Там наливают бесплатно, если сделать ставку.
examples.trans: They pour for free if you place a bet.
The bets are placed, no more bets.

meanings.note: сто пятьдесят = a hundred and fifty; сто рублей = a hundred roubles

examples.trans: I've got a hundred and ten.

examples.text: Понимаешь, Аркаша, мы все скидываемся на этот кластер. Мне москвичам сегодня надо отдать сто пятьдесят.
examples.trans: You see, Arkasha, we're all chipping in for this cluster. I have to give the Moscow people a hundred and fifty today.

meanings.note: 'что я за мэр такой' = what kind of mayor am I
Secondary conversational sense ('? = what's this?') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Russian determiner/pronoun ('your') agreeing in gender, number, and case with the noun phrase it specifies.

examples.text: Я бы на твоём месте подумал.
examples.trans: If I were you, I'd think about it.

meanings.note: High-frequency Russian pronoun ('you') whose case form reflects its grammatical role in the clause.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: Dad, did you bring any gum?

meanings.note: the noun after it is genitive plural: тысячи мест

examples.text: Мы построим кластер. Это тысячи рабочих мест.
examples.trans: We will build the cluster. That means thousands of jobs.

meanings.note: Russian preposition meaning 'at' that governs a specific oblique case on the following noun phrase.
Secondary conversational sense ('I have') (possession) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('from (ask from someone)') (просить у кого) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Привет! Смотри, что у меня есть.

meanings.note: Manner or predicative adverb in '-о' derived from the corresponding adjective stem, used in everyday speech to mean 'well'.
Secondary conversational sense ('good, fine') (as an answer) used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.text: Хорошо, Виктор Петрович, я сейчас же всё переделаю заново!
examples.trans: All right, Viktor Petrovich, I will redo everything right now!

meanings.note: Russian imperfective verb expressing ongoing, habitual, or repeated action meaning 'to want', forming an aspectual pair with 'захотеть'; conjugates for person and number in the present/future and agrees in gender in the past tense.

examples.trans: If you don't want to, suit yourself.
They want to build a shopping centre there.

meanings.note: Used as an imperfective (ongoing/repeated action) verb meaning 'to joke', paired with 'пошутить'.

examples.text: Шутишь? Правда, скажи, где деньги? Меня наняли.
examples.trans: Are you joking? Seriously, tell me, where's the money? They hired me.

meanings.note: pointing at a thing or a situation; 'это' + noun = 'this is ...'
points at something: это моё = that's mine
Secondary conversational sense ('is') (linking word: главное — это народ) used in spoken Russian dialogue.
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:') used in spoken Russian dialogue.

examples.trans: And this is for you. A toy car!

meanings.note: меня = me (genitive/accusative), мне = to me (dative)
Secondary conversational sense ('other forms:  (gen/acc),  (dat),  (instr),  (prep)') used in spoken Russian dialogue.
